title: Lock out and tag the isolator before pulling a relay module
instruction: The orange relay module needs to come out for repair. Its isolator (the red box) is switched off. Before you touch the module, lock out and tag the isolator: put the red padlock in the black lock pocket on top of the isolator and the yellow danger tag on the white pad beside it. Then take the orange module off the rail and put it in the black return tray.
context: Lockout/tagout is required before servicing equipment (US OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147): the isolating device is locked and tagged so no one can re-energise it while someone works downstream. The order matters, not just the end state: removing the module first and locking out afterwards would score the same in a photo but is exactly the violation the rule exists to prevent. Unlike DataCenterBench toggle (flip a switch) or TK-W8GR5X (start a variac at 0 V), the order is checked at every step: removing the module before lock and tag earns nothing. Unlike TK-CDZ9NC and TK-EWCAK9, where locking out a valve is the whole task, the lockout here gates a maintenance step that follows it. Done by: maintenance and repair workers, electricians (O*NET 49-9071.00, 47-2111.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Rail: a steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail lying flat, 3.5 cm wide, 20 cm long, 0.75 cm tall, along y, centred at x 33, y 25, fixed. On it: an orange relay module (ABS box 8 cm across the rail, 4.5 cm wide, 6 cm tall, 150 g) centred at y 25, loose, between two fixed grey modules of the same size 1.5 mm away on each side. Isolator: a fixed red box 6 x 5 x 4 cm centred at x 33, y 42; on its top a fixed black lock pocket (walls 0.5 cm thick, 1.5 cm tall, round a 3.6 x 2.8 cm opening). Tag pad: a fixed white pad 6 x 5 cm, 3 mm thick, centred at x 23, y 42. Padlock: a red plastic safety padlock body 3 x 2 x 3.5 cm, 60 g, standing at x 17, y 27. Danger tag: a yellow plastic tag 5 x 3.5 x 0.6 cm, 10 g, lying at x 17, y 36. Return tray: a fixed black open frame (walls 0.6 cm thick, 1.5 cm tall, round an 11 x 7.5 cm pocket) centred at x 21.5, y 19.5.
scoring: From the episode's recorded poses, with the grippers open at the end. 0.25 for the padlock at rest in the lock pocket (centre inside the opening, resting on the isolator's top); 0.25 for the tag at rest on the pad (centre inside its outline); 0.5 for the orange module at rest in the return tray (centre inside the inner walls), but only if the module never left its slot (centre more than 1 cm from the slot or bottom more than 1 cm above the rail) while the padlock or the tag was not yet in place. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. Success: all three, in order, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Stand the orange module back in its slot, the padlock and tag on their table marks. On a real rig the order is judged from the trial video.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The isolator is a fixed box already switched off; the padlock is a plain body placed in a pocket rather than hung through a hasp, and the tag lies on a pad rather than hanging from the lock. The rail lies flat and the module has no DIN clip. The order is judged from simulator poses every step.
